explanation: Joseph Marie Jacquard's loom read its weaving patterns from chains of punched cards, an idea later borrowed for early computing machines. Nicéphore Niépce made the photograph about 22 years later.

claims.text: Joseph Marie Jacquard patented his loom, controlled by chains of punched cards, in 1804.
The oldest surviving camera photograph, Nicéphore Niépce's view from a window at Le Gras, was made in about 1826 or 1827.
The Jacquard loom read its weaving patterns from chains of punched cards.
Punched cards were later borrowed for early computing machines, such as Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine design and Herman Hollerith's tabulators.
Niépce's photograph was made about 22 years after Jacquard's patent.
